title: Severe Bleeding: What To Do
blurb: The basics of stopping heavy bleeding with firm pressure, calling 999 and spotting shock until help arrives.

cards.title: Severe Bleeding: What To Do
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- recognise severe bleeding and act fast
- apply firm pressure and call 999
- spot the signs of shock and keep the casualty comfortable

cards.title: Minutes matter
cards.body:
Most cuts at work are minor, but occasionally, with knives, glass or powered equipment like the grounds machinery, a wound can bleed heavily. Severe bleeding can become life-threatening in just a few minutes.

Stay calm. Your quick action is what matters most.

cards.title: Firm, direct pressure
cards.body:
The single most important action for heavy bleeding is firm, direct pressure on the wound.

Press hard with a clean dressing, cloth or even your gloved hand, and keep pressing. Do not keep lifting off to look.

items.title: Keep pressing
items.text: Do not lift off to look.

cards.title: Add, do not remove
cards.body: If blood soaks through, do not remove the first dressing. Add another on top and keep up the pressure. Where possible, wear gloves to protect yourself.

cards.title: Call 999 straight away
cards.body:
Call 999 immediately for serious bleeding, or get someone else to while you keep pressure on.

If we have a bleed-control kit and you have been trained to use it, a trauma dressing or tourniquet can be life-saving for a limb that will not stop bleeding. Use these only within your training.

items.title: Trauma dressing or tourniquet
items.text: Only if trained to use it.

cards.title: Keep them still, and watch for shock
cards.body:
Keep the casualty still and reassure them. Watch for shock, which shows as pale, cold, clammy skin and fast breathing. Lie them down and keep them warm.

> If you would like the hands-on skills, tell your manager, as we run first aid training.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Firm, direct pressure on the wound is the first action
- Do not lift off to look. If it soaks through, add another dressing
- Call 999 immediately for serious bleeding
- Use a tourniquet or trauma dressing only within your training
- Keep them still, lay them down, keep them warm and watch for shock

cards.q: What is the single most important action for heavy bleeding?
options: Firm, direct pressure on the wound
Raising the wound above the heart and waiting
Washing the wound out thoroughly first
Giving the casualty a drink of water
cards.why: Firm, direct pressure on the wound is the single most important action.

cards.q: Severe bleeding can become life-threatening within minutes.
cards.why: It can become life-threatening in just a few minutes, so act fast.

cards.q: Blood is soaking through the first dressing. You should:
options: Remove it and start again with a clean one
Add another on top and keep pressing
Stop pressing to let it clot
Swap places with a colleague and take the dressing off
cards.why: Do not remove the first dressing. Add another on top and keep up the pressure.

cards.q: You should call 999 immediately for serious bleeding.
cards.why: Call 999 straight away, or get someone else to while you keep pressure on.

cards.q: The casualty has gone pale. Which is a sign of shock to watch for?
options: Pale, cold, clammy skin or fast breathing
A flushed face and slow breathing
Dry warm skin and calm breathing
A loud voice and a lot of movement
cards.why: Watch for pale, cold, clammy skin and fast breathing.

cards.q: You should keep lifting the dressing off to check the wound.
cards.why: Keep pressing and do not lift off to look.

cards.q: A tourniquet or trauma dressing should be used:
options: By anyone who finds one, at any time
Only within your training
Never, on any wound
Only if the casualty asks for it
cards.why: These can be life-saving but should only be used within your training.

cards.q: You should wear gloves to protect yourself where possible.
cards.why: Where possible, wear gloves to protect yourself.

cards.q: Someone showing signs of shock should be:
options: Sat upright and given a hot drink
Left alone to rest
Laid down and kept warm
Walked around to keep them alert
cards.why: Lie them down and keep them warm, and keep them still and reassured.

cards.q: Powered grounds equipment is one thing that could cause a serious bleed.
cards.why: Knives, glass and powered equipment like grounds machinery can cause heavy bleeding.
